value:
Unparseable store files (#215 step 1): src/utils/unreadable.ts is the vocabulary (StoreUnreadableError, code STORE_UNREADABLE, messages, the bootstrap block) and holds the registry listUnreadableFiles(). directoryStore.ts detects; storage.ts, both wrappers (instrumentation.ts, mcp-server.ts), context.ts, lint.ts and confirm.ts surface.

GOTCHAS:
- listUnreadableFiles lives in unreadable.ts, fed by registerUnreadableSource from store.ts, NOT exported from store.ts: ~10 suites vi.mock('../store') with explicit factories, and a new named export there fails them at link time ("Export named ... not found").
- It does no I/O: it reports what scans this process already ran. That is nearly every command, because resolveKey loads the alias map, which scans both stores.
- Write guards read the target file fresh (probeEntryFile / readSidecar) — scanAndSync fast-skips on an unchanged directory mtime.
- storage.ts getValue/setValue wrap the fast path in a catch-all that falls through; the typed error must be rethrown there or get becomes "not found" and set falls into save().
- save() throws after the odd epoch bump, so it writes the even epoch back first. setOne reads the existing file BEFORE the bump.
- A destination pre-read (set/copy/rename) uses getValueForWrite so the message is the refused write, not a failed read.
- save() is called once per FILE, so its guard is per save, not per command: `set k v -a alias` wrote the value before the alias map refused. Multi-file commands (set -a/--confirm, rename, rm; CLI and MCP) call assertSidecarsWritable BEFORE their first write. It takes a resolver callback and steps aside if that throws, so PROJECT_UNRESOLVED stays the error.
- hasConfirm stays LITERAL. The run gates add confirmListUnreadable() to fail closed; rename uses hasConfirm to decide whether to move a flag, and a fail-closed 'yes' there made it write the conflicted list after the value had moved.
- New exports go in unreadable.ts for the same reason as the registry: '../alias', '../confirm', '../storage' and '../store' are all vi.mock'ed with explicit factories somewhere. mcp-server.ts may only import names those mocks already have.
- Classify conflict vs parse only AFTER JSON.parse fails: a valid value can contain marker lines.

KNOWN GAPS: with an unreadable alias map, `set <alias>` creates an entry named after the alias (not destructive); `data reset` leaves unreadable files in place. One full-suite run stalled with no output during this work and never reproduced — cause unknown.
